submissions.findingTextShort: Human pomegranate studies administer juice or extracts and characterize ellagitannin metabolism; they are not isolated-punicalagin efficacy trials.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Human pomegranate studies including PMID 15309440 administered pomegranate juice rather than purified punicalagin and characterized ellagitannin bioavailability and metabolism. Product-level food or extract exposure must remain distinct from isolated-punicalagin intervention evidence, and these pharmacokinetic/metabolism findings do not establish therapeutic efficacy of the isolated molecule.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy human volunteers consuming pomegranate food or extract products
submissions.usageContext: Pomegranate-product pharmacokinetics and metabolism rather than purified-punicalagin treatment
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The studies establish product/metabolism context but do not isolate punicalagin as the causal intervention.

submissions.findingTextShort: Ellagic acid and microbiota-derived urolithins detected after pomegranate ingestion cannot be back-projected as intact-punicalagin systemic efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Punicalagin and related ellagitannins undergo hydrolysis and downstream metabolism to ellagic acid and microbiota-derived urolithins. Detection of downstream metabolites after pomegranate ingestion must not be represented as proof that intact punicalagin reached systemic circulation, nor may metabolite-associated outcomes be automatically reassigned to the isolated parent molecule.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Metabolic lineage supports relationship edges, not alias equivalence or automatic causal attribution.

submissions.findingTextShort: A branded pomegranate whole-fruit extract trial standardized to punicalagin did not significantly change overall gut diversity and cannot be treated as isolated-punicalagin efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 38201042 tested Pomella whole-fruit pomegranate extract standardized to 75 mg punicalagin for four weeks, not purified punicalagin. Overall gut microbial diversity did not significantly change and the reported between-group urolithin increase was not statistically significant. Product identity, null findings, supplier context and commercial provenance must remain attached rather than being collapsed into an isolated-punicalagin efficacy claim.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy adults receiving a branded multi-constituent pomegranate whole-fruit extract
submissions.usageContext: Branded botanical-product microbiome and metabolite outcomes
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The formulation contains multiple constituents and the short trial does not establish isolated-punicalagin clinical efficacy.

submissions.findingTextShort: Human skin and other pomegranate-product trials standardized by punicalagin content do not close the direct isolated-punicalagin efficacy, safety, or dose gap.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Human trials such as PMID 36431201 administer standardized pomegranate extracts in which punicalagin is a marker constituent. Standardization to a stated punicalagin amount does not make the constituent the tested monotherapy. Direct isolated-punicalagin human efficacy, safety and defensible dosing therefore remain unresolved and product-level outcomes must not be inherited by the molecular owner.
submissions.populationContext: Human trials of standardized multi-constituent pomegranate products
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This finding constrains evidence propagation and recommendation eligibility rather than proving absence of all biological activity.
